THIS TABLE IS NEVER SUMMED WITH C3's. Two rules, two tables, no combined number.

verdicts.link: this declaration must produce exactly one contract link, to the named target, with the named resolution_method. Producing none is a false negative; producing one to another target is a false positive.
verdicts.unresolved: the form is supported and fully understood, and it reaches no registered neighbour. It must produce NO link and must be reported with the named reason. A link here is a false positive.
verdicts.unsupported: the form is one Nerve declines to read. It must produce no link and must be tallied with the named form. A link here is a false positive; a silent drop is a defect even though it is not a false positive.
verdicts.declined_true_link: the declaration names the registered neighbour by an explicit path, and the form is outside the enumerated syntax. Nerve declines it, records it with the form named, and this file counts it as a FALSE NEGATIVE. That is 10b's `Views.handle` rule: a rule that declines a shape declares the miss rather than quietly resolving it, because resolving it would mean supporting a syntax nobody decided to support. A link produced here is not a false positive — it names the right repository — but it means the oracle is out of date and the test fails loudly rather than silently improving the score.

declarations.name: lib-core
declarations.why: a file: dependency naming a directory that is a registered neighbour. The match is made on the repo_id read out of that directory's own index, not on the name 'lib-core'.

declarations.name: lib-extra
declarations.why: workspace: states no path. The path comes from this manifest's own workspaces array ('../lib-extra'), and the member is identified by the name its own package.json declares. Both steps are stated declarations; the registry match is still by repo_id.

declarations.name: ambiguous-dep
declarations.why: one identity declared twice, naming two different repositories. Both links are recorded and neither is promoted: picking a winner would be Nerve inventing the answer the manifest declined to give.

declarations.name: lib-peer
declarations.why: peerDependencies is read on the same terms as the other two sections. The key is the identity; it does not have to match the target's own package name.

declarations.name: lib-inside
declarations.why: the path resolves inside `app` itself. An intra-repository dependency is not a cross-repository contract, and reporting it as an unregistered neighbour would send the user to register their own repository.

declarations.name: lib-missing
declarations.why: the missing-target case. Nothing is at the path; nothing is claimed about what used to be.

declarations.name: lib-unregistered
declarations.why: the negative case, and the one that matters most. A real, indexed, adjacent Nerve repository named by an explicit file: path still produces NO link, because registration is an explicit mutating command and nothing is auto-discovered.

declarations.name: left-pad
declarations.why: an exact version is still a registry resolution. 'left-pad in two repositories may be two packages' is §1's own example.

declarations.name: aliased
declarations.why: an alias names the registry package 'lib-core', which is also the name of a registered neighbour. It must still produce no link: a name is not a path.

declarations.name: linked
declarations.why: link: names a path, and that path is a registered neighbour. A human reading this manifest would call it a local dependency, so declining it is a real miss and it is published as one. It is recorded with its form named, so adding support later is a decision rather than a discovery — and this is the cost of a gate set for zero false positives, stated rather than bought back by widening the syntax.

declarations.name: workspaces[0]
declarations.why: expanding a glob is a resolution rule Nerve would be inventing. The entry is declined with its form named rather than expanded or ignored.
